h1: The 7 Best Lefant Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lefant Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best Lefant robot vacuums of 2026, from the budget M210 to the LiDAR M210 Pro OMNI and self-emptying M3.
summary: The Lefant M210 Pro OMNI is the best of the range, with LiDAR navigation, 20000Pa suction and a self-cleaning roller mop. The M3 is the hands-off dock pick, the M310 Ultra is the value LiDAR robot, and the M330 Pro handles clutter. The M2 Plus adds a 75-day dock, while the M210P and M210 serve thin and entry-level needs.
intro: Lefant names its robots like firmware versions, and that is a trap. An M210, an M210P, an M210 Pro and an M210 Pro OMNI share most of a name and almost nothing else. One is a thin budget vacuum, another adds a few features, and the OMNI is a different class altogether, with laser navigation, a self-cleaning roller mop and a 20000Pa rating. Reading the number on the box tells you very little about what is inside.

Seven Lefant models are ranked here by navigation, dock design, suction, mopping and price tier, drawing on listing details and owner feedback instead of bench figures. Each pick is placed by what it adds or gives up against the model above it, which is the only honest way to rank a family where the names mislead. Pa figures are rated values from the listings, comparable within the range only.

products.name: Lefant Robot Vacuum and Mop, LiDAR Navigation, M210 Pro OMNI
products.verdict: Lefant's most capable robot, with LiDAR and a self-maintaining mop.
products.description:
The M210 Pro OMNI is the model that justifies the Lefant name. It lists LiDAR navigation with obstacle avoidance, 20000Pa suction, a self-cleaning roller mop with auto drying, an 800ml dustbin and 5G WiFi, in the $200 to $500 tier. Laser mapping lets the robot plan straight rows and remember rooms, and a mop that cleans and dries itself removes the sour-pad problem.

It ranks first because it carries the full navigation and self-maintenance set that cheaper Lefants skip. The M3 below offers a longer emptying claim but lists no LiDAR.

Buy it if you want Lefant's best. The caveats are price and size: it is the most expensive Lefant here, and the dock has a large footprint, so check you have a spot against a wall for it.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting Lefant's most capable navigation and mop.

products.name: Lefant Robot Vacuum and Mop, 12000Pa Suction, 90-Day Self-Emptying, M3
products.verdict: A 90-day dock and hot water mop washing without flagship pricing.
products.description:
The M3 is the hands-off pick. It lists 12000Pa suction, a 90-day self-emptying dock, a hot water self-cleaning and drying dock for the mop, and 5G WiFi with Alexa, app and iWatch control, in the $100 to $200 tier. Hot water washing of the mop pad is rare at this price, and a dock that empties the bin spares you the daily chore.

It ranks second because it delivers the dock automation of the OMNI for less, but without LiDAR in the listing. The 90-day figure is a claim that assumes light debris.

Buy it if you want to stop handling the bin and the mop. The caveat is navigation: the listing does not describe how the M3 maps rooms, so check owner comments on routing before you buy, especially in a multi-room home.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a hands-off dock for less.

products.name: Lefant M310 Ultra Robot Vacuum and Mop with ToF LiDAR Navigation
products.verdict: ToF LiDAR navigation and a slim body at a mid-low price.
products.description:
The M310 Ultra is the value navigator. It lists ToF LiDAR navigation, 6000Pa suction, a slim profile and a 170 minute runtime, with vacuum and mop functions, in the $100 to $200 tier. Time-of-flight laser sensing gives accurate room maps without the OMNI price, and 170 minutes of runtime covers a large floor on one charge.

It ranks third because suction is lower than the M3 and the listing shows no dock, so you empty the bin yourself. It beats the M330 Pro on how precisely it navigates.

Buy it if route accuracy comes first and you do not mind handling the bin. The caveat is the missing dock, so over weeks you will empty it often in a pet home. The slim profile helps under furniture, though no height figure is given.
products.idealFor: Buyers who put navigation accuracy first.

products.name: Lefant Robot Vacuum and Mop, Upgraded 190° PSD Obstacle Avoidance, M330 Pro
products.verdict: Obstacle avoidance matters more than suction in a messy home.
products.description:
The M330 Pro is the clutter specialist. It lists 190 degree PSD obstacle avoidance, a 450ml visible dustbin, a 150 minute runtime and multi-floor mapping, in the $100 to $200 tier. PSD sensors detect objects ahead to steer around cords and pet toys, which is where many robots fail.

It ranks fourth because its strength is avoidance rather than power, and it carries no dock or LiDAR. The M310 Ultra navigates more precisely, but the M330 Pro is the one that spares you picking up the floor first.

Buy it for homes with cords, pets and everyday clutter. The caveat is that you empty the bin by hand and the listing does not highlight suction, so heavy carpet is not its strength. Multi-floor mapping helps if the robot moves between levels.
products.idealFor: Homes with cords, pets and floor clutter.

products.name: Lefant Robot Vacuum and Mop, 75-Day Self-Emptying, 6000Pa Powerful Suction, M2 Plus
products.verdict: Stop emptying the bin by hand, at a budget dock price.
products.description:
The M2 Plus has the second-longest dock claim in the range. It lists a 75-day self-emptying dock, 6000Pa suction, a 140 minute runtime and 2.4G and 5G WiFi with Alexa, app and iWatch control, in the $100 to $200 tier. For people tired of emptying a bin, a dock is the main reason to pay.

It ranks fifth because the M3 offers a 90-day dock and mop washing for the same tier. The M2 Plus is the simpler dock option, with basic mop care.

Buy it if you just want a dock and no daily emptying. The caveat is the mop: care is basic, so you still wash the pad yourself. If self-washing matters, the M3 is the better buy for the same money, and the 75-day figure is a best-case claim.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a basic dock and no daily emptying.

products.name: Lefant M210P Robot Vacuum Cleaner, 4000Pa Suction, Super Thin
products.verdict: A super thin robot with a 200 minute runtime for tight clearance.
products.description:
The M210P is the thin one. It lists 4000Pa suction, a super thin profile, a 200 minute runtime and app, WiFi and Alexa control, in the $100 to $200 tier. A low body slides under beds and sofas that stop taller robots, and 200 minutes is the longest runtime in this ranking.

It ranks sixth because it is vacuum only, with no dock and no mapping detail. What it adds is the runtime and the thin body, which matter in a small home with low furniture.

Buy it if clearance under furniture is the problem. The caveat is that no exact height is listed, so measure your lowest gap and compare with the manufacturer's page before ordering. Skip it if you want mopping or a dock, since the M2 Plus costs the same tier.
products.skipIf: You want mopping or a dock.

products.name: Lefant Robot Vacuum Cleaner, M210
products.verdict: The cheapest, simplest way into Lefant.
products.description:
The M210 is the entry point. It lists self-charging, app and WiFi control, multiple cleaning modes and a low-profile design, in the $50 to $100 tier. For a first robot in a small apartment, it keeps the cost low and the setup short.

It ranks last because the listing gives no suction, runtime or dock figures, so you cannot compare it with the others on numbers. It is the lowest-priced pick here, and the name resembles the M210P and the M210 Pro, which causes mistakes.

Buy it for a small apartment where you want a basic vacuum on a tiny budget. The caveat is that very little is documented, so confirm the exact model on the page and read recent owner feedback before ordering. Do not assume it has the OMNI's features.
products.idealFor: Small apartments and first robot buyers.
products.skipIf: You want documented power or mapping.

whatMatters.detail: Lefant uses letter and number combinations like M210, M210P, M210 Pro and M210 Pro OMNI for very different machines. A suffix can mean thinner, stronger or an entirely different class. Read the bullet list for navigation and dock details, and ignore the model number as a quality ranking, since the letters hide big hardware gaps.

LiDAR measures walls with a laser to map rooms, while PSD sensors detect objects ahead to avoid collisions. LiDAR gives better route planning, and PSD helps with cords and toys. Check which problem your home has most, and note that the OMNI and M310 Ultra list LiDAR while the M330 Pro lists PSD, so match the sensor to the problem.

Lefant lists 75 and 90 day dock intervals. These are claims for ideal use, and pets and carpet shorten them. Treat them as best case, check the bin or dock bag early, and plan to empty sooner in a home with shedding animals or lots of dust, because a full bin cuts suction.

Pascals measure suction force, and the range here runs from 4000Pa to 20000Pa. Higher helps on carpet and pet hair, but compare within the Lefant range rather than across brands, because makers rate suction differently. Check whether the figure is a maximum mode that drains the battery fast, shortening the quoted runtime.

Thin models like the M210P help with low furniture, but listings often give no exact height. Measure your lowest gap and compare it with the stated figure, if any, and allow a margin for rugs. A robot that nearly fits will still get stuck and stop mid-clean, and you come home to a dead robot under the bed.

faq.a: The M210 Pro OMNI and the M310 Ultra list LiDAR navigation. The M330 Pro uses PSD avoidance, and the other models list simpler sensing. Check the bullets before buying, because the names do not tell you which have laser mapping.

faq.q: What is the biggest Lefant buying mistake?
faq.a: Assuming model numbers rank quality. An M210P and an M210 Pro are very different robots, so compare the listed features rather than the name. Look at navigation, dock and mop first, and treat the suction number as a secondary guide.

faq.q: Is the OMNI worth it over the M3?
faq.a: If you want LiDAR and self-cleaning mop care, yes. The M3 gives a 90-day dock and hot water mop washing for less, so choose navigation or price. The OMNI also adds an 800ml dustbin and obstacle avoidance.

faq.q: How do I set up a Lefant robot?
faq.a: Place the charger by a wall, connect to 2.4G WiFi, or 5G where supported, and use the app. Run a first clean with doors open, then set schedules and no-go areas in the app so it avoids pet bowls and cords.

Clean the brush, filter and sensors regularly and empty the bin or dock bag. Wash mop parts where applicable. Pet homes need more frequent care than the dock claims suggest, with the brush checked for hair weekly.

Higher suction models cope better, but check the listing for carpet notes. Mop models should avoid thick rugs. Test on a small area first, and lift fringes out of the way so the brush does not catch them.

finalTake: Buy the M210 Pro OMNI if you want Lefant's full navigation and mop automation, or the M3 for the dock features at a lower tier. The M310 Ultra is the navigation value, the M330 Pro suits cluttered homes, and the M2 Plus is a plain dock. The M210P and M210 are for tight furniture and tiny budgets.
